content:
incident-bot: ALERT: High tail latency and elevated 5xx for Kepler VPC (dp-kepler-2). Severity: P1. Trigger: p95 latency > 1.5s and 5xx > 4% for 4m. Link: https://infra.redwood/alerts/2956789012 :rotating_light:
Priya: Acked. Paging @Sam (oncall). Pulling scheduler logs and placement table now.
oncall-bot: @Sam is oncall until 2026-03-16 14:00 UTC. Please update channel every 8 minutes.
Sam: Oncall here. Early look: several dedicated nodes show GPU memory overcommit warnings and the kube-scheduler reports pods being scheduled onto nodes with insufficient reserved memory for committed tenants. I'm seeing a recent config push 03:02 UTC that changed reservation labels for a subset of jobs.
Lee: Quick context: Kepler recently added a bursting batch job from their analytics team which was supposed to land on a separate burst pool, but I see the job's nodeSelector incorrectly set to "pool: dp-kepler-2". That explains cross-contam.
Sam: Reproduced the errors in logs: kernel OOM like evictions + runtime rejecting requests with 503 when cache can't be allocated. Correlates with client spikes from kepler-analytics account.
Priya: Can we cordon and drain the mis-scheduled analytics pods while we redirect live traffic? Prefer to isolate rather than immediate node reboot.
Sam: Agreed. Steps: cordon affected nodes, migrate committed VPC pods to standby pool, throttle non-committed analytics job. Executing now.
Sam: Commands executed:
```
# cordon nodes to block new scheduling
kubectl cordon node/gpu-node-11 node/gpu-node-12
# evict analytics pods (best-effort)
kubectl drain node/gpu-node-11 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force --grace-period=30s
# redirect routing for kepler API traffic to standby dp-kepler-standby
redwoodctl routing set --from dp-kepler-2 --to dp-kepler-standby --percent 90
```
Sam: After routing change: p95 latency dropped from 1.8s to 420ms over 60s. 5xx fell to 0.6%. Evictions reduced.
Priya: Good. I notified Kepler account team (cc @Jen-CS). Jen, please prepare a holding message explaining we performed an emergency isolation and are investigating root cause.
Jen-CS: On it. Drafting now. Suggest offering temporary commit credit and a post-incident technical review.
Sam: We should also note that the analytics job was mis-tagged; ask customer if they intentionally updated their job spec. Could be a pipeline change on their side or a misapplied IaC template.
Lee: I grabbed the recent IaC diffs. There's a pipeline merge at 02:58 UTC that added "nodeSelector: pool: dp-kepler-2" in the analytics workflow. I'll add the diff to the incident ticket.
Priya: Immediate mitigations checklist for post-incident: 1) enforce admission control on committed pools to reject pods without right tenant labels 2) add alerting for sudden cross-tenant scheduling events 3) backfill scheduling reservations for dedicated pools.
Sam: Filing infra bug: RB-9812 "Admission webhook to enforce pool tenancy for committed pools" and linking to this thread.
Sam: We need a customer-facing timeline for impact. Preliminary estimate: degraded HTTP success rates for dp-kepler-2 between 02:57 and 03:25 UTC (~28 minutes). Peak 5xx ~9%. Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/stream and /v1/embeddings endpoint for some requests. No indications of data leakage.
Jen-CS: DRAFT CUSTOMER NOTE:
```
Subject: Immediate update  Kepler VPC dp-kepler-2  Incident observed 2026-03-14

Hi Kepler team,

We're investigating an incident affecting your dp-kepler-2 dedicated pool. Summary: between 02:5703:25 UTC we observed elevated latency and 503 errors caused by a mis-scheduled analytics job that consumed reserved GPU memory on nodes servicing your committed VPC.

What we did immediately:
- Detected the anomaly via automated alerts and paged oncall.
- Cordoned affected nodes and drained non-committed analytics pods.
- Redirected traffic to your standby pool dp-kepler-standby to preserve capacity.

Current status: traffic is stabilized and metrics returned to normal at 03:25 UTC. We are continuing root-cause analysis and will share a full RCA.

Proposed next steps and compensation:
- We propose issuing 48 hours of Dedicated pool credit applied to your account.
- Offer a technical runbook review and a session to harden your IaC job templates.
- Share the RCA and scheduling policy updates within 5 business days.

Apologies for the interruption. We take committed capacity seriously and will follow up with concrete mitigations.

Best,
Jen (Redwood Customer Ops)
```
Priya: Please add that we will implement an admission webhook to prevent this class of mis-scheduling and will share the implementation timeline.
Jen-CS: Added.
Sam: Ops note: as a short-term mitigation, enabling strict reservation enforcement on dp-kepler-2 now (toggle applied). Monitoring shows no regressions.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity lowered to P2. Please attach post-incident tags and create RCA ticket.
Priya: Action items assigned: 
- Sam: confirm PR for reservation enforcement toggle and schedule canary (PR by EOD; canary tomorrow).
- Lee: supply IaC diff and link merge request that caused mis-tagging.
- Jen-CS: send customer holding note now and propose time for exec sync; include 48h credit offer.
- Priya: draft full RCA and scheduling policy change doc within 5 business days.
Sam: I'll also add per-pod memory usage alert and a new alert rule for "pods scheduled on committed pools without tenant label".
Jen-CS: Sent holding note to Kepler ops and cc'd accounts. Requested a 30-min ops review tomorrow 14:30 UTC.
Priya: Thanks team. We'll keep this channel as the source of truth for the RCA timeline and follow-ups. Closing incident once RCA posted and customer exec sync scheduled. :white_check_mark:
Sam: Linking infra bug RB-9812 and IaC MR here: https://git.redwood/rb/9812 and https://git.redwood/mr/kepler-analytics-142
Jen-CS: Noted. Will confirm when credit applied and customer call scheduled.
oncall-bot: Handoff recorded. Current status: stabilized. Incident will remain open pending RCA delivery.
